name: A Theology of Marriage and Parenting

objectives.text: Identify the family as a gift God gives and name the members of a family
Recite the fifth commandment and name ways children honor their father and mother
Retell how God created the first man and woman and brought them together as husband and wife
Give examples of how children obey and honor their parents at home
Identify from Psalm 127 that children are a gift and blessing from the Lord
Explain what Genesis 2:24 means by leaving parents, holding fast to a spouse, and becoming one flesh
Describe how family members in Bible stories showed loyal love and forgiveness to one another
Explain the callings Ephesians 5 gives to husbands to love sacrificially and to wives to submit, as the Reformed tradition reads the passage
Explain the duties Scripture gives parents to instruct, nurture, and correct their children without provoking them
Explain how Jesus pointed back to creation when he taught about marriage
Compare the household and the church as communities in which God gives order, care, and instruction
Explain how honoring parents extends to adult children caring for aging parents
Explain the purposes of marriage named in the Westminster Confession and the Scriptures that support each
Analyze how Ephesians 5 presents marriage as a picture of Christ and the church
Interpret Deuteronomy 6 on parents teaching God's words to their children in the ordinary rhythms of daily life
Explain the Reformed teaching that covenant promises extend to the children of believers and how this shapes infant baptism and parental vows
Analyze the families of Isaac, Jacob, and David to show how favoritism and sin damaged the household
Explain the biblical purpose of parental discipline as loving correction aimed at wisdom and maturity
Explain how the seventh commandment guards marriage by requiring sexual faithfulness in thought and deed
Construct a biblical definition of marriage as a covenant between one man and one woman
Explain the biblical teaching that believers are to marry only in the Lord
Explain how Scripture honors singleness as a calling for serving the Lord
Explain what Scripture teaches about divorce and summarize the position of the Westminster Confession
Evaluate cultural redefinitions of marriage and family against Scripture and the church's confession
Defend the Reformed tradition's teaching that man and woman are equal as image bearers and distinct in their callings in marriage
Design a plan for family worship that includes Scripture reading, prayer, and singing, grounded in Scripture and Reformed practice

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (marriage as God's design, honoring parents, leave and cleave, Ephesians 5 roles, family and church, children as blessing, Christ and church, Deuteronomy 6, discipline, definition of marriage, cultural redefinitions, complementarity, family worship). Dropped vague items such as observing love in the home and replaced the abstract covenant faithfulness item with an analysis of biblical family narratives and a covenant children objective. Added missing competencies: parental duties, Jesus on marriage, care of aging parents, purposes of marriage, the seventh commandment, marrying in the Lord, singleness, and divorce. Anchored objectives to specific verses and to WCF 24, WCF 28.4, WCF 21.6, WSC Q10, Q63, Q64, Q71, WLC Q129, and HC Q74, Q104, Q108-109.
